video_title: AI Bubble + Rising  Rates = Time For Caution | Jim Iuorio
gist: Futures trader Jim Iuorio calls the AI trade a concentrated bubble layered on rising 10-year yields, and hedges with puts and collars while staying invested. He expects the 10-year capped near 5.5% by eventual Fed long-end buying, favors debasement assets, and forecasts disinflation and Fed cuts in 2027, with France and Japan bond stress as a contagion watch item.

insights.claim: Iuorio calls the AI trade a mania/bubble but notes that identifying a bubble is worthless for timing since one can be three years early; his guess is the music stops 8 to 18 months out, with the exact timing unknowable.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Argues for staying invested with hedges rather than exiting; sets a rough 2027 risk window.
insights.quote: you can identify a bubble as it's inflating and still be 3 years too early

insights.claim: Market breadth is poor: only about 25% of stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, while the 7 biggest stocks made up 35% of S&P market cap in May, versus 25-26% at prior peaks in 2001 and 1980.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Record index concentration means index-level risk is really single-theme AI risk.

insights.claim: A cited headline says Micron and Nvidia alone will deliver about a third of S&P Q3 earnings growth while the median stock barely grows, so the market revolves around a thinner axis.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Any stumble in two names can drive a material index correction.

insights.claim: Micron rallied roughly 300% in 8 weeks, which Iuorio treats as clearly abnormal and a sign to de-risk winners.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Parabolic semis moves are a profit-taking and hedging cue.
insights.quote: When Micron rallies 300% in 8 weeks time

insights.claim: Large 20%+ corrections have tended to begin when the VIX is low, around 15-16, per Iuorio's research; he reads the low VIX as complacency and cheap protection, and holds roughly 3x his normal put size.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Cheap vol is the time to buy protection; VIX may be distorted by options proliferation.

insights.claim: Iuorio exited SMH and replicated it with a short ATM 5-week call, three longer-dated calls, and one converted to a call spread, capping downside while keeping upside exposure after big gains in Micron, AMD and SMH.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Example of keeping AI beta with defined risk instead of selling outright.

insights.claim: He sees no sign yet of mom-and-pop leveraging like 2000 (tech) or 2007 (multiple homes), which suggests the bubble may have time to run; margin debt is high but unclear whose it is.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Absence of retail leverage argues against an imminent crash; lack of margin-debt composition data is a gap.

insights.claim: Taggart notes retail equity allocations are near record highs and rise with age cohort, the opposite of prudent allocation, which raises downside vulnerability.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Older cohorts heavy in equities amplify a drawdown's wealth-effect hit.

insights.claim: Iuorio argues proliferation of zero-day options raises short-term volatility but is not a systemic risk, and may make markets more durable by wiping out reckless speculators early.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Contrarian dismissal of 0DTE systemic risk.

insights.claim: Iuorio says retail is no longer 'dumb money': tools are about twice as sophisticated as institutions had 20 years ago; he reports a new type of call asking how to buy 10-year bonds.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Anecdotal early sign of retail interest in duration at ~5%+ yields.

themes.theme: Treasury Yields, Fed and Debasement Trade

insights.claim: Iuorio lists four drivers of rising 10-year yields: heavy bond issuance to fund deficits and conflicts (most underappreciated), inflation (secondary), foreign central banks trying to leave dollars, and AI competing for investment dollars.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Supply and competing capital demand, not just inflation, are pushing term premium.

insights.claim: He worries yields rise but does not believe they will: he caps the 10-year near 5.5% because the Fed would eventually buy long-end bonds and sovereigns and hedge funds would buy at 5.3%+.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Defines a ceiling around 5.5% on the 10-year; supports starting to add duration.

insights.claim: Scott Bessent has three times since August 5 signaled he wants to burn bond shorts; Iuorio expects him to wait for the trade to turn and then push with it, as currency interventions only work with the trend.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: A Treasury squeeze on bond shorts could add to a yield reversal; crowded short-bond positioning is a risk.
insights.quote: I think he's waiting in the wings for for the trade to start to mean revert

insights.claim: The Fed has expanded its balance sheet by about $200 billion over roughly eight months by buying bills and facilitating Treasury bill sales; growth has leveled off in the last month but is not being drained.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Stealth balance sheet expansion is already underway despite hawkish rhetoric.

insights.claim: If the Fed starts buying long-end bonds, he wants to be long the debasement trade: gold, silver, platinum, real estate, farmland and possibly Bitcoin; probability is meaningful but not high conviction.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Fed long-end intervention is the trigger to watch for a rebound in hard assets.
insights.quote: Now, that's not a high conviction it's going to happen right away

insights.claim: Iuorio would expect Kevin Worsh to reverse on balance sheet purchases only if the 10-year nears 5.5%, Nasdaq falls about 35% and S&P about 25%, and the economy looks much weaker; he puts it as less likely than the 70% he would assign to Powell.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Gives explicit pain thresholds for a Fed put under Worsh.

insights.claim: Worsh's recent 25bp hike into a supply-shock inflation, with Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 5.1%, was in Iuorio's view signaling credibility more than effective policy.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Hike was cheap credibility; the Fed is not tightening into weakness, so pivot risk exists.

insights.claim: The wealth effect from asset prices over six years is a major economic driver, so an AI-stock correction would hit the economy; Taggart adds AI capex flows would also dry up, an economic one-two punch.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Market and economy are linked; AI drawdown is a macro risk, not just equity risk.

insights.claim: Iuorio sees no fiscal restraint from the Trump administration and says spending continues like a drunken sailor, supporting debasement assets; he thinks Illinois bonds trade with implicit federal backing.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Deficit path supports gold and hard assets; muni credit may carry implicit federal support.

themes.theme: AI Productivity, Labor and Inflation Path

insights.claim: Iuorio says US productivity gains since early 2023 exceed even the 1997-2003 internet adoption period, convincing him AI is a lasting disruptive force even if the equity trade ends.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Supports owning AI real-economy winners long term while fearing valuations.

insights.claim: Taggart notes missing evidence: earnings calls rarely cite AI adoption raising corporate profits by 20%; if that evidence does not appear, tech CTOs will cut capex.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Capex return on investment is the key swing factor for AI hardware demand.

insights.claim: Unlike 2001 dot-com names that went to zero, today's AI leaders were profitable before the boom and are earning more because of it.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: A bust would be a valuation reset, not a business-model collapse.

insights.claim: Taggart cites Keynes on technological displacement and fears tens of millions displaced faster than they can be redeployed, with robotics compounding it; Iuorio agrees and links it to socialist candidates winning elections, but expects adaptation within about two years.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Labor displacement is a political and policy risk; populist backlash is a second-order effect.

insights.claim: Iuorio argues adaptation is faster than expected, citing how oil supply routes were rerouted in eight months despite analyst claims it would take ten years.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Supports a faster-than-consensus labor and supply adjustment.

insights.claim: Iuorio expects disinflation to dominate by roughly Q3 2027: oil supply shocks turn recessionary within 8-14 months, Fed hikes lag 8-14 months, and AI deflation outweighs AI buildout inflation; he expects rate cuts about four to five months into 2027.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Gives a timeline for the pivot to cuts and favors duration into 2027.

insights.claim: Iuorio notes the UAE left OPEC to add about three million barrels a day and Venezuela is coming online, which could push oil sharply lower if the Iran situation settles.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Supply additions and a resolution could remove the inflationary oil impulse; a $10-15 oil drop would help the economy.

insights.claim: Iuorio keeps about 15% of his investment portfolios as dry powder, relies on options to finance entries later, and has trimmed 20-30% of gold and silver positions after the January run, seeking re-entry.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Shows a practitioner taking profits in precious metals while waiting for lower entries.

insights.claim: He is heavily overweight healthcare (XLV bought from about 150 at his newsletter) as a defensive sector AI may make more efficient, and is considering buying 10-year Treasuries for the first time instead of staying within two years.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Rotation from AI toward defensive sectors and duration.

insights.claim: Iuorio cut real estate from four properties to two as profit-taking and says he is open to municipal bonds but has not done enough work.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Muni interest is a gap worth research.

insights.claim: Reshoring and strong manufacturing numbers, new expensing tax rules, deregulation and foreign direct investment could lift the economy if oil falls, even though Iuorio opposes tariffs as a free trader.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Domestic cyclical upside exists if oil drops.

insights.claim: Yields in France and Japan are spiking; Iuorio fears contagion that would hurt US equities via global risk reduction but push US Treasury yields lower as a safe haven.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: A European or Japanese bond selloff is a bearish equity, bullish Treasury setup.

insights.claim: Iuorio says the August episode began with Bessent threatening yen shorts and the carry trade and then supporting the yen alongside the Bank of Japan.
insights.speaker: Jim Iuorio
insights.so_what: Yen carry unwinds are a recurring global liquidity risk.
